name: Hyphen test uses value comparison of a char vs reference comparison (==) of String objects
side_a: No deduct if the delimiter test compares a primitive char against the literal '-' (e.g. username.charAt(i + 1) == '-'), so the comparison actually evaluates the character's value and the hyphen is genuinely detected.
side_b: Deduct if the delimiter test compares String objects with == (e.g. username.substring(i + 1, i + 2) == "-"), since reference comparison does not test string contents, the condition is effectively never true, and the hyphen-skipping branch never executes.

name: Lookahead access `charAt(i + 1)` (or loop bound reaching length) is guarded against running past the last index vs. left unguarded
side_a: no_deduct: the response only reads positions it has proved are in range — either it never peeks past the current index, or it explicitly guards the peek (e.g. `if (i < username.length() - 1 && ...)`) and keeps the loop bound strictly below `username.length()`. Correct in-range traversal that produces the right shortened string earns B3.
side_b: deduct: the response peeks at `username.charAt(i + 1)` (or equivalent) while `i` can legally be the last index, or runs the loop to `i <= username.length()`, so the method throws StringIndexOutOfBoundsException before returning. A guaranteed runtime exception on a typical valid username forfeits B3 even though the concatenation/return lines are textbook.

name: Detecting the hyphen with a value comparison (char literal / .equals) vs. with `==` on String objects
side_a: no_deduct: the hyphen test compares values — `charAt(i) == '-'` on a char, or `.equals("-")` / `.compareTo` on a substring — so the branch that removes the hyphen actually fires and the returned string is the shortened one.
side_b: deduct: the hyphen test applies `==` to a String expression (e.g. `username.substring(i + 1, i + 2) == "-"`); the reference comparison is false for the runtime-built substring, the removal branch never executes, and the method returns the full unshortened name. This is a logic error in the string-building algorithm, not an excused 'String method called incorrectly'.
